pageCache.pageTitle: North Farnborough Infant School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Nurturing the Future, Inspiring Success
At North Farnborough Infant School, we want to instil a love of learning whilst creating happy, confident and aspirational children who are well-prepared to be good citizens of any community they join.
Our vision and values are at the core of everything we do. They underpin our teaching and learning, and provide an environment which prepares our pupils as happy, confident, safe and successful citizens.
Our Aims:
Develop resilient, positive learners with high aspirations.
Our Core Values:
We respect other peoples’ ideas and belongings.
We work hard to be good listeners.
We use kind and caring words.
We ‘have a go’ at things before asking for help.
We try our best and rise to a challenge, never giving up.
We enjoy achieving together and on our own.
Being kind to others helps us to feel happy in ourselves.
We do the right thing even when no-one is looking.
We make the right choices to keep ourselves and others safe.
Vision and Values

British Values
Promoting British Values
British Values are defined as democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance of different faiths and beliefs. We promote these values through our mission statement, our school values, our class and school charters and curriculum.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to North Farnborough Infant School
It is with great pleasure that we welcome you to our school website.
We are an infant school catering for children from the age of four to seven. During your child's three years with us, we aim to recognise that every child is unique, and we will value each one of them as an individual, providing them with a secure and friendly learning environment in which they can fully develop.
We have a team of talented, caring and dedicated staff who work hard to ensure the best possible progress for all the children in their care.
We look forward to working in partnership with you. Together we will ensure that your child has a happy, safe and successful experience at school and achieves in a way that is personal and fulfilling.
You are very welcome to visit us; I invite you to look at the Admissions page on the website to find out when our next new parents tour will take place and how you can book.
We are very proud of our school and look forward to getting to know you and your child. Lauren English Interim Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: North Farnborough Infant School - NFIS Governors
pageCache.text:
NFIS Governors
On behalf of the Governors, we warmly welcome you to North Farnborough Infant School.
NFIS is a vibrant and joyful school located in the heart of Farnborough. Our governors, staff, parents, and pupils take great pride in our school, the high standards and progress our children achieve, and our strong connections with the local community.
The governing body collaborates closely with our headteacher and senior leadership team to ensure that the school's standards and expectations remain high, and that all our children grow into well-rounded individuals ready for the next phase of their education. While governors are not involved in the day-to-day management of the school, we help set its long-term vision, direction, and ethos. Above all, we prioritise our pupils' safety, wellbeing, and education.
We are fortunate to have a dedicated and hard-working team at North Farnborough who deliver an enriched and creative curriculum, giving every child the opportunity to reach their full potential. We also have incredibly supportive parents who enhance the life of the school by reading to children, organising community events, assisting on educational visits, and raising funds through the Friends of North Farnborough Infant School (FONFIS).
Please enjoy exploring our website, including the governors' pages where you can learn more about who we are, what we do, and how you can get involved. You can contact us via the school office.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Farnborough Infant School - Remote Learning
pageCache.text:
Remote Learning
Remote Education Provision: Information for Parents
During COVID, our priority was to deliver high quality education, whether it be online or in school. We taught the same curriculum remotely as we did in school wherever possible and appropriate. We did make some adaptations to some subjects. For example, some subject areas such as Art and DT required materials that were not readily available to all families at home. In these instances, the class teacher may have blocked a subject that lends itself to remote teaching more easily and then taught the subject areas missed when pupils returned to school.
Post COVID-19 lockdowns and isolations, we have maintained our capacity for remote education. Although we are able to maintain this capacity, remote education will only be considered as a short-term measure and as a last resort where in-person attendance is not possible or contrary to government guidance.
Occasions when school leaders decide that it is not possible for their setting to open safely, or that opening would contradict guidance from local or central government.
Occasions when individual pupils, for a limited duration, are unable to physically attend their school but are able to continue learning, for example pupils with an infectious illness.
In these circumstances, pupils will have access to remote education as soon as reasonably practicable, in proportion to the length of absence and disruption to their learning time, and allowing time for pupils to complete tasks and assignments independently.
The information below provides more information on how Remote Learning will be set / what you can expect if learning was to be moved to an online format again in the future.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum
At North Farnborough Infant School, we believe every child is unique and should be empowered to become a responsible, independent learner with a lifelong love of learning. Our curriculum is built around our CARE principles – Curiosity, Achievement, Resilience, and Excitement—which is woven into everything we do, both in and out of the classroom.
At our school, we aim to ignite curiosity by encouraging children to ask questions such as "Why?" and "How does this connect?" We create an environment where learning is driven by exploration and the desire to understand the world around them. Throughout all our subjects, curiosity questions are used as the basis of our learning, with every lesson, answering a key aspect of the overarching question. This approach develops enquiring minds that see learning as an exciting journey of discovery, sparking a sense of wonder that lasts a lifetime.
Achievement is at the heart of our curriculum. We celebrate each child’s progress, regardless of their starting point, and ensure our children experience the maximum sense of success. By setting high expectations and providing tailored support where appropriate, we empower our children to reach their full potential. Achievement is not just about academic outcomes at North Farnborough, but also about personal growth, confidence, and the satisfaction of overcoming challenges along the way.
We place great emphasis on resilience, teaching children to embrace challenges, learn from setbacks, and to never give up. Our curriculum supports the development of perseverance, encouraging children to bounce back from mistakes and see them as opportunities for growth.
Resilience isn’t just about bouncing back; it’s about bouncing forward, adapting, and growing stronger in the face of adversity. As a school we use the mantra ‘I can’t do it yet!’......
Above all else, we aim to make our learning exciting and enjoyable for our children. Our curriculum is designed to be creative, engaging, and fun, ensuring that each lesson sparks joy and inspires children to approach learning with enthusiasm. By connecting lessons to real-world experiences, we make sure learning feels relevant and enjoyable, building confidence, independence, and a deep love of learning. This excitement drives children to take ownership of their learning and develop the skills they need for life beyond school.
Through the CARE principles, we prepare our children not only for the academic challenges of the future, but for the opportunities, responsibilities, and experiences of life. North Farnborough fosters an appreciation of mutual respect, equality, and diversity, helping children grow into well-rounded individuals who are ready to contribute to a global community.
We offer a curriculum that:
Is creative, exciting and engaging.
Enables pupils and teachers to make the most out of every learning opportunity and create lifelong learners.
Promotes the spiritual, moral, cultural, mental and physical development of pupils at the school and of society
Prepares pupils at the school for the opportunities, responsibilities and experiences of later life
Is valued because it is fun to teach and inspires independence, resilience and confidence.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Farnborough Infant School - English as an additional language (EAL)
pageCache.text:
English as an additional language (EAL)
North Farnborough Infant School has a diverse and multicultural community; over fifteen different langauges are spoken.
We recognise the uniqueness of every child based on their skills, attitudes, needs and life experiences. We value our rich multicultural school, and we embrace the opportunities that this provides for all our children. We recognise that not all children arrive at school fluent in English and are aware of all the different cultural aspects of British life.
This leaflet explains why we ask parents for information about a child’s first language: it is used to help the teachers give the best support possible to your child.
We celebrate cultural diversity and understand the advantages of being bilingual. We also recognise that if a child develops good use of home language, they are in a better position to achieve high competence in English and succeed in school. We appreciate how much you can help your child do well in school by reading and talking to them in the home language.
Please choose a leaflet below to find out more about bringing up children bilingually.
